**Commercial Controller**

**Function**
Finance, FP&A

**Location**
Dubai

**Reports to**
Senior Financial Controller

**Purpose**

Owns the money side of the buy, from the annual plan to realised margin. Sets the budget and margin target, approves the order book against them, grants Buying its budget to buy, and reports where the season landed against plan. Finance's single point of control on what the company commits to buy.

**Where the role sits in the chain**

Sales Operations controls demand and delivers a matched order book: PO quantities against sales orders,delivery dates, declared MOQ overage. The Commercial Controller gates the money on that book. After Book Handover the chain executes; this role monitors and re-opens only on exception.

**Responsibilities**

**Plan and budget**

* Build the annual commercial plan with the Senior Financial Controller: revenue, buy budget, intake margintarget and inventory envelope by brand, channel and season
* Maintain the plan through the year; update it after each order book with actuals, revised forecast and variance

**Margin**

* Build and maintain landed cost by style: FOB, freight, duty, royalty and licensor minimums
* Set and maintain intake margin targets by brand, channel, customer and season
* Analyse margin by style against the price list and customer terms; margin by style is the basis of approval

**Approval of the buy**

* At order book validation, approve or reject the matched book: margin against target, value against budget, cash against the forecast
* Document each approval and each rejection with the reason, for CEO sign-off
* Grant the OTB to Buying per master PO, sold buy and MOQ overage shown separately

**Control after approval**

* Hold any PO that exceeds the granted OTB and return it to validation
* Track price and cost variance from approval through supplier confirmation to GRN
* Monitor inventory value, cover and ageing by brand and season; flag breaches into the next validation

**Reporting**

* Weekly: approvals, OTB granted, open holds, variance and inventory, to the Senior Financial Controller and Sales Operations
* Season end: bridge planned to realised margin after cancellations, returns, claims, discounts and overage disposal, with drivers
* Input to board reporting and the group forecast on buy, margin and inventory

**Decision rights**

* Approves or rejects the order book on budget, margin and cash. Grants the OTB. Holds POs over OTB.
* Escalates to the Senior Financial Controller on target changes and to the Group CFO where plan, margin or cash are at risk.

**Not in scope**

Demand, PO-to-SO matching, delivery dates, assortment, buy quantities, supplier negotiation, OTB planning, any approval after Book Handover.

**Interfaces**

Senior Financial Controller (line) · Sales Operations (order book) · Buying and Supply Chain (OTB, variance) · FP&A Senior Analyst (plan and forecast) · Group CFO (escalation).

**Measures**

Budget adherence of the buy · intake margin delivered against target · approval turnaround at validation · variance explained from approval to GRN · inventory value and ageing within envelope · plan accuracy.

**Requirements**

• 4–6 years in commercial finance, FP&A or merchandise finance in fashion wholesale or retail

• Landed-cost modelling, intake margin, margin bridge, OTB and inventory maths

• ERP and planning-tool literacy; strong Excel; Business Central an advantage

• Builds a budget and defends it; rejects a buy and writes do

**Role Summary**

The Payroll Specialist (IC2), based in the UAE, is responsible for ensuring accurate, timely and compliant payroll processing for Greece (primary market) and for supporting payroll operations in Jordan, Iraq and the UAE. This role covers the full payroll cycle: auditing employee records, maintaining payroll data integrity, calculating and validating payroll, ensuring adherence to Labor, tax, and social security laws, and supporting continuous improvement in payroll processes and reporting. Deep working knowledge of Greek payroll is required; for the other countries the specialist must know how to process payroll using local rules and guidance from local advisors, without needing to be a full local expert.

**What’s On Your Plate?**

* Employee Data Audit: Review and verify all newly onboarded and status-changed employees in the payroll system (including AMKA, AFM tax number and bank details) to ensure data accuracy and completeness.

* Compliance Management: Ensure payroll processing aligns with Greek Labor Law, Income Tax (AADE) and Social Security (e-EFKA) regulations, and with the applicable Labor, tax and social security requirements in Jordan, Iraq and the UAE, as well as company policies. Implement any regulatory or policy changes (for example the annual e-EFKA ceiling, tax scale and minimum wage updates) in coordination with technical, functional, People Operations, Legal teams and local advisors.
* Statutory Filings (Greece): Prepare and coordinate the monthly e-EFKA (APD) declaration and payment, withholding tax payment, ERGANI II notifications and annual earnings certificates, working with the local payroll provider or accountant where applicable.
* Local Coordination: Work with Greek HR, local advisors and authorities, and with the local teams in Jordan, Iraq and the UAE, from the UAE, ensuring payroll deadlines, SLAs and legal requirements in each country are met.
* Leave Administration: Review and post leave transactions (annual, sick, maternity and other statutory leave under Greek rules) accurately in the payroll system in coordination with HR.
* End of Service (EOS): Maintain and update end-of-service and severance records in accordance with company policy and Greek legal requirements.
* Payroll Processing: Review and validate all payroll transactions (including off-cycle and regular runs, and the Greek 14-salary cycle: Christmas bonus, Easter bonus and holiday allowance) processed by the team for accuracy and compliance.
* End-to-End Payroll Cycle: Collect and validate monthly inputs (attendance, overtime, allowances, deductions, joiners, leavers), calculate gross-to-net pay, run variance analysis, review the payroll register and obtain approvals before payment.
